newsitem.title: FRANCE: French tobacco firm Seita's profits jump 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: French tobacco firm Seita's profits jump 15 pct.

text.p: French tobacco company Seita said on Thursday profits jumped 15 percent last year, powered by robust export performance, cost cutting and strong investment returns.

The newly privatised company, best known for its pungent Gauloises and Gitanes cigarettes, said net attributable profit rose to 786 million francs from 684 million francs in 1995 on turnover which climbed 6.2 percent to 17.4 billion francs.
Operating profits soared 26.3 percent to 1.2 billion francs.
Financial profits jumped 106 percent to 179 million francs. Exceptional charges totaled 230 million francs against charges of 87 million francs in 1995.
But the company warned that it was worried about prices in 1997.

"Market conditions were generally stable at the start of 1996 but deteriorated at the end of the year due to fresh pressures on prices. For 1997 there is great uncertainty over the question of cigarette prices," the company said in a statement.
Seita president Jean-Dominique Comolli warned of the possibility of a price war fueled by the success of new cut-rate brands, and said he wanted the state to head off such a war.
"I am still hopeful that a reasonable solution can be found in coming weeks," he told a meeting of analysts.
